meta.goal: Strong, lean and fit. Moderate loads, perfect form, a healthy spine.

blocks.name: Foundation
blocks.focus: Learn the movements and find your starting weights. Everything light and smooth — you should finish every set feeling like you had 3-4 more reps in you.

blocks.name: Build
blocks.focus: Moderate weights, tight form. Add reps first, then take the smallest weight step up. Two reps in the tank on every set.

blocks.name: Strong
blocks.focus: A touch heavier, never a grind. If a weight forces you to brace hard or hold your breath, it is too heavy — drop back and own the reps. Week 12 is lighter: 2 sets, enjoy it, then start the next cycle.

variants.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
variants.cue: Feet flat, shoulder blades tucked, only your natural arch. Lower to chest level under control.

alt.name: Incline Dumbbell Press (30°)
alt.cue: Low incline, same tucked shoulder blades. Press up and slightly back.

variants.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
variants.cue: Back pad upright, neutral grip, ribs down. Press without arching the low back.
variants.spine: Keep this light. Overhead work loads the spine — the back pad does the bracing for you.

alt.name: Incline Dumbbell Press (45°)
alt.cue: High incline hits the front delts with the bench doing the bracing.

variants.name: Seated Arnold Press
variants.cue: Light. Start palms facing you, rotate out as you press. Back stays on the pad the whole time.
variants.spine: Lighter than a normal press — the rotation is the work, not the load.

alt.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
alt.cue: Back pad upright, neutral grip, ribs down.

variants.name: Seated Single-Arm Dumbbell Press
variants.cue: One arm at a time, free hand holds the bench. Don't let your torso lean away — that's the core work.
variants.spine: Unilateral so the load is half, and your core resists the side-bend.

alt.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press

variants.name: Cable Chest Fly

alt.name: Cable Chest Fly

alt.name: Cable Chest Fly

variants.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise

alt.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise

variants.name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise

core.name: Dead Bug
core.cue: Low back pressed into the floor the whole time. Slow.

variants.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
variants.cue: LIGHT. Soft knees, hinge at the hips, dumbbells slide down your thighs. Stop the moment your hamstrings tug — never let your back round.
variants.spine: The one hinge in the plan. If your back says anything at all, swap to the hip thrust — same muscles, spine supported.

variants.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust (shoulders on bench)

variants.spine: Zero spinal load. This is the glute exercise for a stenotic back.

options.name: Apple Fitness+ HIIT

options.name: Apple Fitness+ Cycling
options.note: Easiest on the spine. Bike or spin bike at home.

options.name: Apple Fitness+ Rowing
options.note: Only if you row with a tall neutral back — skip if it bugs you.

options.name: Apple Fitness+ Dance or Kickboxing
options.note: Fun beats optimal. Full-body, gets the heart rate up.

options.name: Outdoor Walk / Run
options.note: Time to Walk or Time to Run. Fresh air counts.

core.name: Apple Fitness+ Core
core.note: Do this right after the cardio. Modify: skip sit-ups, V-ups, Russian twists and weighted crunches — swap in dead bugs, planks or bird dogs for those sections.

cooldown.name: Apple Fitness+ Mindful Cooldown or Yoga
cooldown.note: Optional. Skip deep backbends; hips and hamstrings are the priority.

rest.name: Rest
rest.note: 20-30 min easy walk if you can. Optional 10-min Apple Fitness+ Yoga or Mindful Cooldown. Lean happens with daily movement, not just gym days.

rules: Double progression: pick a weight, work up to the top of the rep range on every set, then take the smallest step up and start again at the bottom of the range.
Reps first, weight second. Adding a rep at the same weight is progress.
Every set should end with 2-3 reps still in the tank (RPE 6-8). Nothing in this plan is meant to be a max.

spine: Neutral spine on every rep. If you have to round or arch to move the weight, the weight is too heavy.
Moderate loads only: you should never need to hold your breath and brace hard. Dumbbells and cables, nothing overhead heavy, no barbell.
Prefer supported positions: seated with a back pad, chest on a bench, hand on a bench.
Skip these for good: sit-ups, crunches, V-ups, Russian twists, back extensions / supermans, good mornings, heavy deadlifts, loaded twisting.
Progress by reps first, then the smallest weight step — 5 lb on dumbbells, one plate on cables.
Warm up every time. Two minutes walking before you lift is non-negotiable.
Sharp pain, numbness or tingling down a leg means stop that exercise for the day and swap to the alternative. Check in with your doctor or PT if it repeats.

treadmill.note: Any 20-min Treadmill session that alternates walking and running. Mostly Z2, a little Z3.
Hiking-style: incline up, speed down. Zero impact, big heart rate. Great when legs are heavy.
Run pushes at Z3-Z4, walk the recoveries. The one that makes you fitter fastest.
A continuous easy run at a pace you could talk through. Z2-Z3 the whole way.
Brisk walk with incline changes. Swing the arms, stay tall. Perfect recovery cardio.
Pushes that get longer then shorter (1-2-3-2-1 min). Z3 building to Z4 at the peak.
Jogging with incline intervals. Legs and lungs together — Z3 on the climbs.

treadmillNote: Legs feeling cooked? Trade today's session for the Incline Walk — the rotation just picks up next time.
